Greetings Goats. For the past several years, I've been working on a new gaming community, user review, and forum platform. I've kept a low profile, but it's officially launched in an open beta.

Instead of writing a regular review that covers everything about the game, you're able to write a small 100 to 750 character review about a specific thing about that game. Examples include things like graphics, music, etc. You can even be very specific and talk about things like boss fights, basic game mechanics, etc. You're allowed to be very specific or very vague, just as long as you stick to a specific topic. You can write reviews and they can be just text, an image, or a video. Not only that, but Game Sense supports all generations of games, so you're free to talk about your favorite retro games. As you can guess, this opens up a lot of possibilities. One of which is that you can write reviews without playing the game, as long as it's clearly something you can see without playing the game. For example, if you've never played a specific game, but you like a song from it, you can write a review about the music. The scoring algorithm is designed to accommodate this. Which is why it has two parts, the actual score and the completion rate. The more complete a review is, the more accurate the score is. All scores also start at 5.

Reviews are categorized by a type. Types can include things like glitches, graphics, music, localization, etc. This lets Game Sense make it easy to read reviews, because you can filter them out by type. If a game has great music, you can see all the great music at once. If it's full of bugs, you can quickly and easily see all the reviews regarding bugs. There's also the "Channels" feature, which will do things like let you see all upcoming reviews that are previews, good music, etc.

There's a lot to the site. I urge you to sign up and start looking around. If you're ready to start writing reviews, one of the best places to start is with one of your favorite games. I'll be around the thread to answer questions for quite some time.

Game Sense is more or less similar to what Voat is to reddit, a place for people who aren't swallowed up in PC culture to talk about games without having to worry about it. I've seen plenty of people banned for making good arguments, but were PC wrong think, and that's not going to fly at Game Sense.

A few frequently asked questions:

What kinds of games are supported? You can add any games that are mature or under. Games like Senran Kagura and Dead or Alive are fine, but more sexual games like hentai are not allowed. They do not have to be mainstream games, they can be indie games or even projects you are working on, or have completed. Though we ask that if you submit your own game, you don't review it, only submit news. And when sharing your Game Sense page, you can't tell people to write good reviews. You can tell them to share their thoughts on the game but not to ask for good reviews. The way Game Sense works, that will end up hurting your score in the long run. There's actually been some demand for a sister site that allows adult and hentai games and the plan is to make it.

What makes Game Sense different from other user review sites? It's more informal, straddling the line between a forum and a review site. Not to mention the reviews only focus on a specific thing, which makes it easier to discuss the game as well as to categorize reviews by type and to create things like the Channels, or specific feeds of reviews of specific types, which makes it easy to show people specific things about a game, like if it's poorly localized, has good music, etc. You can also filter reviews based on what platforms you are interested in or you can specifically follow new games. When you log in, you'll be notified of how many new games were added, how many games on each platform you're interested in were added, and how many you follow have been updated with new reviews or news.

The open beta only started last night, so it's just getting going. We're looking forward to seeing your opinions on games and the other things you can review. It's an open beta, so there might be some issues. I'll keep an eye on everything and be fixing stuff quickly. Feel free to provide feedback is anything is confusing, or if you think some categories are missing or anything.

[Game Sense](https://gamesense.co)

EDIT: There's also an official Twitter account: https://twitter.com/GameSensedotCo I'd appreciate it if anyone with Twitter would help signal boost. Instead of begging for money, the site was personally funded, so Game Sense is at a little disadvantage compared to sites that have money from gaming interest groups.

Thanks for sharing your site with the /v/gaming community. Granularity by specific game elements isn't something I've seen applied to reviews before, but I like the concept. And I'm always in favor of crowd-sourced reviews. What do you anticipate will be the biggest challenge for Game Sense moving forward?

Right now it will be getting a solid community going with gamers who really care about games. People's responses really exceeded my expectations so far, but the quality community is the hard part. And I'm aiming for a top quality community that is really passionate about games, specially ones who are a bit disappointed with how things are going with games. Response has been great so far for the little bit I've been mentioning it. Normally you expect one or two people per every one hundred that check it out to sign up, and it's been much better than that.

From there, the goal is to bring in developers who can talk directly with gamers and address specific issues that are good or bad about a game, and fix them with community input. Not to mention another goal is for developers to be able to promote and discuss their games, specially the ones that normally don't get the media coverage they deserve.

It sounds like you've identified some realistic goals and challenges alike. Eventually bringing in developers would be an incredible endgame because it would dis-intermediate traditional games media in a meaningful way. Connecting developers directly with gamers has benefits for both. In the meantime, I'm glad you're seeing some uptake; it must be a great feeling to watch your project grow. I noticed there are some sections of the search in addition to just games (gaming sites, youtubers, platforms, etc); what gave you the idea to include these categories as "review-able" items along with the games themselves?

It's a very great feeling, thank you. The idea of reviewing those other websites came from the fact that gamers have been more interested in making sure they're getting news from a quality source. There's a lot of really nasty things going on in a lot of internet media, like positive reviews for possessions, money, etc. and it's not being disclosed properly. And I wanted to make a place for gamers to hold some of the less ethical outlets accountable for their actions. Not to mention the news aggregator takes into account a site's score and prioritizes news sites in good standing.

Someone to watch the watchmen, so to speak :) I think it's a great concept, and I hope you get all the community support you need. Projects like this live or die by their communities, but I think you're taking all the right steps to encourage more people to contribute. Thank you again for sharing with the /v/gaming community, and particularly for sticking around to answer a few questions.

Possible Heart Benefits Of Taking Estrogen Get Another Look

The authors of the WHI study intentionally overstated their results to "make a difference". Their study actually found that women who are past menopause that start hormone therapy have an increased heart risk. There was no indication that women who continued therapy or started during menopause had any increased risk.

That's important context; I appreciate you weighing in.

There was no indication that women who continued therapy or started during menopause had any increased risk.

Do you mean the possibility that the risk may decrease again some time into treatment?

The prior thinking was that hormone replacement therapy (HRT) reduced cardiovascular risk for women at and beyond menopause. The WHI study showed that this is not true for women who wait until after menopause to start HRT. The study did not show any specific risk or benefit for women who start taking HRT during menopause and continue after menopause.

The study in the article is examining the effect of HRT in women younger than those that were found to be at higher risk in the WHI study.
